hypothesis: The Riemann-Roch (Nagao) relation encoding, compiled by Weil descent to F_2 and handed to an XOR-native SAT solver, is a decomposition oracle on the ECC2K-130 curve whose exhaustion cost grows with the factor-base dimension d at an exponent below that of brute-force pair enumeration (2 in |F|), and it does so at a lower cost than the matched Semaev S'4 system under the same solver on the same instances.
prediction_written_before_the_run: Both parts fail. (1) Under Weil descent the two encodings are LINEARLY equivalent: the X^3 and X^0 coefficient equations of the norm form, b + b^2 = r + e1 and c^2 + b^2 = r e3, are F_2-linear in (a, b), so the function coefficients are affine images of the elementary symmetric functions of the summands plus one free bit, and XOR-Gaussian preprocessing reduces the RR system to S'4 with extra columns. The RR encoding will therefore cost at least as much as S'4 under every solver, and more where the solver must carry the 131 coefficient variables. (2) The linear NO-certificate of solver_14/15 (affine span of the S4 value set proper for d <= 6, saturated from d = 7) will be visible as refutation with essentially no search for d <= 6 and will vanish at d = 7; beyond it the SAT search will grow faster than 4x per dimension, i.e. faster than |F|^2, so the fitted exponent of the SAT cost in 2^d will be ABOVE 2, not below it. Decompositions of uniform targets begin to exist at d = 45 (m l >= 131 + log2 m!), so every uniform instance in the panel is expected UNSAT and measures exhaustion, never yield.
curve_and_field: K_0 : y^2 + xy = x^3 + 1 over GF(2^131) in the POLYNOMIAL basis F_2[t]/(t^131 + t^8 + t^3 + t^2 + 1) (lowest-weight irreducible found by curves.findIrreduciblePoly; irreducibility re-checked by field.Pb.isIrreducible). Group order verified equal to 4r with the published 129-bit prime r = 680564733841876926932320129493409985129 (curves.curveOrder). The factor base is V = { x : deg x < d } \ {0}, i.e. the span of the first d polynomial-basis vectors, restricted to abscissae that lift. This is Trimoska's layout and differs from solver_10..15's ONB span only in the choice of the d-dimensional subspace; the counting boundary and the null object depend on |F| alone.

encodings.s4: Trimoska S'4: variables x1,x2,x3 (3d bits, ids 1..3d), auxiliaries e1 (d), e2 unreduced (2d-1), e3 unreduced (3d-2) defined from the x bits, then the 131 coordinates of S4(E1,E3,E4) = e3'^4 + (e4'+1) e3'^2 + e4'(e4'+1) e1'^2 + e1'^4 on {x1,x2,x3,x(R)} (the elementary-symmetric form frozen in solver_06/15). Validated by reproducing the published instance Xn15l5-1-S.anf equation for equation (test_weil.TrimoskaReproductionTest) and by exhaustive tiny-field oracles.
encodings.rr: Nagao norm form: f = x^2 + a x + c + b y in L(4O), f(-R) = 0, N(X) = A(X)^2 + bX A(X) + b^2(X^3+1) matched to (X+r)(X+x1)(X+x2)(X+x3). Variables x1,x2,x3 (3d bits, ids 1..3d), beta (1 bit), a (131 bits). b is eliminated symbolically: E1 (b + b^2 = r + e1) is F_2-linear with kernel {0,1}; b = H(r + e1) + beta with H the half-trace, valid under the single emitted trace equation Tr(r + e1) = 0. E2, E3, E4 are emitted in full (3 x 131 equations). a is NOT eliminated although E4 makes it affine in (b, e3): keeping the function's x-coefficient as a free variable block is what makes this the Riemann-Roch encoding rather than S'4, and it is the one design freedom the encoding has left under descent. Validated against a numeric solver of the same equations and the group oracle on every triple of a tiny field (test_weil.RREncodingTest); RR witnesses are shown to be a subset of S4 zeros and to exclude non-lifting (twist) configurations by construction.
encodings.rr_full_not_run: The literal norm form with b as 131 free variables has the bilinear product ab with 131^2 = 17161 monomials. WDSat allocates xorgauss_equivalency_history[MAX_ANF_ID][ID][ID/64] statically, about 12 GB at that size on a 16 GB host, so it cannot be built; under CryptoMiniSat it is 17161 extra Tseitin gates that XOR-Gaussian elimination removes at preprocessing. The b-eliminated form is the same system after the elimination the solver would perform first.

solvers.cms: CryptoMiniSat 5.15.0 via pycryptosat, single thread, native XOR clauses (one per equation) plus one Tseitin AND per non-unary monomial. Complete and sound on every tiny-field and pilot instance. PRIMARY cost measure: the smallest conflict budget (confl_limit) at which the solver decides the instance, found by doubling then bisection on fresh solvers over identical input, which is deterministic for this build (pilot: two independent brackets agreed). Bracketing is attempted only when the plain solve completes within 30 s; otherwise the conflict count is null and the wall time stands as a censored lower bound of the cost.
solvers.wdsat_plain: WDSat at upstream commit 61c6ff3f49445af2729274819edb27b85a89efc1 (the frozen regression-suite source), rebuilt per (encoding, d, mode) with config.h sized exactly from the instance (the sizing reproduces Trimoska's own IC-S4 l=6 constants 52/767 at d = 6), no -x, with -b. Complete on every pilot planted instance (6/6 permutations enumerated without -b at d = 4,5,6). Its decision counter conf (the unit the regression suite calls wdsat_conflicts_v1) is recorded as the brute-force tree control: the pilot shows it equal to 2^(3d)/3! to within 0.1 % at d = 7 (349,857 vs 349,525), i.e. no pruning. Run on s4 only: on rr its -b mode returns a false SAT with the coefficient block unassigned (the block is not definitional), and without -b it exceeds the budget at d = 7.
solvers.wdsat_xg_audit: WDSat -x (XOR-Gaussian elimination during search) is run on PLANTED instances only, as a completeness audit, never as a cost. The pilot found it INCOMPLETE at n = 131: with FIND_ALL it returned 4 of 6 permutations of a planted triple at d = 6, and with -x -b it returned UNSAT (51 decisions) on a decomposable target, while the same solver with the abscissae fixed by unit clauses accepted every permutation and refuted a non-solution, and over-allocating every static array changed nothing. The defect is in backtracking, not propagation. Any -x cell that fails to find a planted relation is recorded as a solver completeness failure.

null_object: Brute-force pair enumeration over the factor base: for each unordered pair of admissible abscissae {x1, x2}, compute R - P1 - P2 for the sign choices and test membership of the abscissa in V. Cost unit: C(A, 2) pairs, A the number of admissible abscissae in V (measured exactly per d). solver_12 measured this control at 0.494x the field operations of the best RR solver at d = 6 and solver_13 fitted its exponent at 2.06 in |F|. It is the boundary every SAT cost here is read against.

boundaries.existence_threshold: m l >= 131 + log2 m! gives l = 45 at m = 3; every d in this panel is far below it, so uniform instances measure exhaustion cost and planted instances measure the cost of finding a relation that provably exists.
boundaries.counting_ceiling: P(uniform target decomposes) <= min(1, C(B+2, 3)/r) with B = 2A stored points; at d = 10 that is below 10^-32.
boundaries.rho_reference: S = 0.077 at 2^60.8 group operations (RESEARCH_ECC2K130_RR_SOLVER_PANEL.md section 1). No S, Lambda or rho ratio is computed from this panel and none would be meaningful at d << 45.

panel.seed_note: Fresh. Pilot and calibration used 20260920, 777 and 4242 and are development data (pilot.json); no pilot target is reused.

modes.uniform: single decision (UNSAT proof = exhaustion of the candidate space)
modes.planted: first solution, then enumeration by blocking each found abscissa triple until UNSAT, up to 64 witnesses

panel.budget_note: Wall budget on a 4-vCPU x86_64 Linux host; a TIMEOUT is censored, retained, and never read as negative evidence (AGENTS.md section 6 of the parent contract).

correctness_gate: Every SAT witness is re-verified independently of the solver: the 3d abscissa bits are lifted with CurvePb.pointFromX (x = 0 mapped to the 2-torsion point), and the eight sign choices are summed in the group; a witness counts as a relation only if some choice gives x(P1+P2+P3) = x(R), and as a genuine relation only if in addition the abscissae are distinct, nonzero and different from x(R). A planted instance decided UNSAT by a solver configuration, or a completed planted enumeration that misses the planted triple, is a completeness failure of that configuration and voids its cost figures for the round. A uniform instance decided SAT with a verified genuine relation would be a decomposition of a random ECC2K-130 point at d <= 10 (probability below 10^-32) and would invalidate the round's target minting.
falsification: The hypothesis SURVIVES this round only if, for at least one encoding under a complete solver configuration, (i) at least four d values have every uniform instance decided within budget with a measured conflict count, (ii) the least-squares slope of log2(mean conflicts) against d over those sizes is below 1.8 with the four-point fit's residual standard error below 0.5, and (iii) for rr specifically, its conflict count is at most 0.8x the s4 count on every matched instance. Anything else falsifies it: a slope at or above 2 closes the SAT route as an exponent lead on this system; rr costing more than s4 on matched instances closes the coefficient encoding as a lead under SAT. The prediction above says both closures will occur.
inadmissible: Reading a TIMEOUT as UNSAT, as a cost, or as a relation count.
Fitting an exponent through censored cells or through fewer than four complete sizes.
Comparing a complete run against a truncated one (the solver_12 CORRECTION.md error).
Using WDSat -x figures as costs, or WDSat -b figures on the rr encoding at all.
Reporting wall time as the headline; conflicts and decisions are the units, wall time a practicality note.
Treating the planted stratum as a yield estimate.
deliverables: raw.jsonl (one record per solver cell, append-only)
RESULTS.md with the single table and the classification
classification_rule: By AGENTS.md section 3 of the crypto repository: an exponent below 2 in |F| for a complete solver would be an ADVANCE candidate pending independent replication; a lower constant at the same exponent is ENGINEERING; a lower headline count with a higher total is RELABELLING; a changed number with an unchanged algorithm is ACCOUNTING. The expected outcome is a measured negative with a named, measured obstruction (the saturation of the S4 value-set span at d = 7 and the super-quadratic growth of the SAT search beyond it), which under the inventor protocol is a closure of the exact tested scope and nothing wider.

predecessor_and_position.predecessor: research/notes/ecc2k130/RESEARCH_ECC2K130_WDSAT.md (#498, merged 2026-09-20): the RR incidence and norm encodings exported from the circuit IR (full-field ONB Weil restriction, thousands of variables) in front of WDSat and CryptoMiniSat at n = 5 and n = 9. Its section 7 names three things that would make another round worth running: (1) a subspace factor base of dimension l in Trimoska's layout so the instance fits under WDSat's ~23 M monomials_to_column ceiling; (2) a conflict counter for the CryptoMiniSat arm so the cross-solver comparison can be made in the declared unit; (3) __FIND_ALL_SOLUTIONS__ so the oracle is priced on every root.
predecessor_and_position.how_this_round_answers_them: (1) weil.py descends in a polynomial basis with V = {deg x < d}: S'4 is 9d-3 variables and RR (b eliminated) is 3d+132, both orders of magnitude under the ceiling, and it runs on the real n = 131 curve rather than a toy field. (2) cmsConflictBracket recovers a deterministic conflict count for CryptoMiniSat by bisection on confl_limit, so the primary unit is available on the complete solver. (3) planted instances are enumerated to UNSAT (WDSat FIND_ALL builds; CryptoMiniSat by blocking clauses).
predecessor_and_position.what_this_round_adds_that_the_predecesso: The predecessor's WDSat figures are all from SAT instances, where an incomplete search that happens to reach a witness looks identical to a complete one. The pilot here shows WDSat -x is incomplete at n = 131 (false UNSAT on a decomposable target with -b; 4 of 6 permutations without), so its 1,277x conflict reduction on RR-norm cannot be read as an exhaustion cost; this round treats -x as an audit only and measures exhaustion with a solver shown complete on every planted instance.
predecessor_and_position.exporter_note: ecc2k130/codegen/wdsat.py exports an ir.Prog circuit; weil.py writes ANF from exact symbolic Boolean polynomials and needs no circuit. The parity convention (emit T exactly when the polynomial's constant term is 0, so the asserted XOR-to-one clause states p = 0) is the same one the predecessor's section 4.4 and wdsat_oracle.rs arrived at, and is checked here by reproducing Trimoska's published instance.
